issues.title: Inconsistent Chinese translation for 'Name' field across namespaces
issues.description: The PR updates the Chinese translation for 'Name' from '称呼' to '姓名' across multiple translation files to ensure consistency. However, this change creates a cross-namespace inconsistency issue. In ghost.json, line 31 shows 'Name' translated as '名字' (first name), while in portal.json line 117 it's translated as '名称' (generic name/title). This inconsistency will confuse Chinese users when they see different terminology for the same 'Name' field between email templates (using ghost namespace) and the portal UI (using portal namespace). The correct translation should be '姓名' (full name) consistently across both files as intended by the original PR.

issues.title: Missing interpolation variable in newsletter unsubscribe message
issues.description: The translation for the key '{memberEmail} will no longer receive {newsletterName} newsletter.' in portal.json is missing the {newsletterName} interpolation variable. The Chinese translation only includes '{memberEmail}将不会再收到新闻信。' which omits the newsletter name placeholder. This means when users unsubscribe from a specific newsletter, they won't see which newsletter they're unsubscribing from, leading to confusion and potential accidental unsubscriptions. The translation should include both {memberEmail} and {newsletterName} variables to match the English source and maintain functional parity.

issues.title: Translation inconsistency for 'Enter your name' field across UI contexts
issues.description: The PR introduces an inconsistency in the Chinese translation for the 'Enter your name' input field. In portal.json line 71, it's translated as '输入您的名字' (enter your first name), which suggests only a first name is needed. However, based on the context of Ghost's user registration and profile system, and the fact that the 'Name' field itself should be '姓名' (full name), this creates a mismatch between what the label asks for ('名字' - first name) and what the system actually expects ('姓名' - full name). This can cause user confusion during registration and profile completion, potentially leading to incomplete or incorrectly formatted name entries.

issues.title: Deletion of comments.json breaks comments-ui build for Chinese locale
issues.description: The PR deletes ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json, but this file is required by the comments-ui application build configuration. In apps/comments-ui/vite.config.mts line 56, the Vite build explicitly declares dynamicRequireTargets for comments.json across all SUPPORTED_LOCALES, including 'zh'. When the build system attempts to bundle the Chinese locale translations, it will fail because the required comments.json file no longer exists. This will break the build process for the comments-ui application or cause runtime failures when users try to view comments in Chinese.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25696 - Align zh translations with China mainland terminology.

structured_output.summary:
This PR edits Simplified Chinese (zh) i18n strings to use mainland terminology: "会籍" becomes "订阅" across subscription messages, "评论" and "名字" are standardized, and the empty "Subscription details" key in ghost.json is finally translated. Most of the wording changes are readable and an improvement, and the text-only scope means no runtime code is touched.

However, the diff deletes `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json` outright (74 lines, all comments-app strings). The PR description says this file was refined, not removed, and I confirmed at head that the file no longer exists while every other locale still ships a `comments.json`. That is a regression for Chinese readers of the comments widget, and it must be resolved before merge. There is also a meaning regression in the portal "will no longer receive newsletter" string, which drops the `{newsletterName}` placeholder, and a small terminology split where "Name" is "名称" in portal.json but "名字" in ghost.json, which contradicts the stated goal of consistent naming.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The unexplained deletion of zh/comments.json is a correctness problem: the PR description says the file was refined, but the diff removes it entirely, so the comments widget loses its zh translations. That alone blocks merge. The dropped {newsletterName} placeholder and the Name terminology split are smaller but should be fixed in the same pass, since the PR's stated purpose is consistency.

architecture.overview:
Ghost ships its UI strings as per-locale JSON namespaces under `ghost/i18n/locales/<locale>/`. The loader in `ghost/i18n/lib/i18n.js` exposes namespaces such as `ghost`, `portal`, `comments`, `search`, and `signup-form`, and each frontend app (Portal, the comments widget, the admin-facing ghost strings) requests the namespace it needs. Translations are plain key-to-string maps where the English key is the lookup key and the value is the translated string, so editing a value changes rendered text without touching any code path.

This PR only edits values in the zh namespace files `ghost.json` and `portal.json`, and it deletes the zh `comments.json` namespace file. Because no code changes, the runtime effect is entirely determined by which keys and files exist for zh after the merge. The deletion removes the whole `comments` namespace for zh, so any comments-app lookup in zh no longer has a zh-authored source.
steps: Entry point: the i18n loader in `ghost/i18n/lib/i18n.js` resolves a locale and namespace (`ghost`, `portal`, `comments`, `search`, `signup-form`) to a JSON file under `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/`.

Two namespaces are edited in place: `ghost.json` switches subscription wording from 会籍 to 订阅, standardizes Comment/Name, and fills the empty "Subscription details" key. `portal.json` reworks email-preference, unsubscribe, and invite-only copy.
The `comments.json` namespace for zh is removed. Every other locale directory still has this file, so zh becomes the outlier. This is the step that needs to be reconsidered.
Terminology is not fully uniform after the change: `Name` is 名字 in ghost.json, 名称 in portal.json, and 称呼 in the deleted comments file. The PR's "consistent 名字" goal is only partly achieved.

findings.title: zh/comments.json deleted, contradicting the PR description
findings.fixPrompt: In the Ghost repo, `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json` was deleted in this PR, but the PR description says it should be refined (consistent 评论/名字 terminology and clearer load/show hints). Restore the file from base commit 96253df and apply the intended wording refinements so it matches the sibling locale files' key set. Verify that its key set matches `ghost/i18n/locales/en/comments.json`. Do not change any other locale files.

findings.title: Newsletter name dropped from the unsubscribe confirmation string
findings.fixPrompt: In `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/portal.json` around line 9, the value for the key `"{memberEmail} will no longer receive {newsletterName} newsletter."` was changed to drop the `{newsletterName}` placeholder, losing which newsletter the member unsubscribed from. Restore the placeholder in the zh value while keeping the new wording, for example `{memberEmail}将不会再收到{newsletterName}新闻信。`. Keep the interpolation variable spelled exactly as in the key.

findings.title: "Name" translated three different ways across namespaces
findings.body:
The PR says it standardizes naming, but the key `Name` now maps to different values depending on the file: `名字` in `ghost.json` (line 31), `名称` in `portal.json` (line 117), and `称呼` in the deleted `comments.json`. Portal also uses `名字` in `Enter your name` and `输入您的名字`, so the same file uses both 名字 and 名称. Pick one term for the form-field label and apply it across namespaces.

::diff{file="ghost/i18n/locales/zh/portal.json" lines="117-117"}
findings.fixPrompt: Standardize the zh translation of the key `Name` across `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/ghost.json` (currently 名字) and `ghost/i18n/locales/zh/portal.json` (currently 名称). Choose one term and use it in both files. Also check that `Enter your name` in `portal.json` uses the same term. Keep the change limited to these values.

findings.title: Subscription details translation filled in
findings.body:
The empty `"Subscription details": ""` in `ghost.json` is now `订阅详情`. This was a real gap in the locale, since an empty value makes the UI fall back or show nothing for that string. The 会籍→订阅 switch is also applied consistently to the subscription messages in `ghost.json`, which is what the PR description intends.
